questions.question: RBI defined M1 as CU + DD. What is DD?

options.text: Net demand deposits held by International banks only
Net demand deposits held by RBI
Net demand deposits held by SBI
Net demand deposits held by commercial banks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__**. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the context of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI) defining M1, "DD" stands for Demand Deposits.**
 
• **Demand Deposits** represent the net demand deposits held by commercial banks.
 
• **Demand Deposits** are a type of bank account from which deposited funds can be withdrawn at any time without any notice to the bank.
 
• These types of accounts include checking accounts, savings accounts, or any other type of bank account that allows for the immediate withdrawal of funds.
 
• They are considered to be highly liquid assets and are included in the calculation of the** M1 money supply.**
 
• **Net Demand Deposits** would account for the total of these deposits held by a bank, minus any amounts that the bank has itself deposited with other banks.
 
• This gives a more accurate view of a bank's liquidity and the amount of money readily available in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) defines various monetary aggregates to measure the amount of money in circulation in the Indian economy.
 
• M1 money supply includes components such as:
 
 
• Currency **(notes and coins in circulation with the public and vault cash of banks) **- denoted as **CU.**
 
• **Demand Deposits of the public (DD) **with commercial banks.

questions.question: What is the full form of FTP?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** FTP** stands for** File Transfer Protocol**.
 
• It's a standard network protocol used for the transfer of computer files between a client and server on a computer network.
 
• FTP is built on a client-server model architecture using separate control and data connections between the client and the server.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are many protocols used in computer networking, each serving different functions and purposes. Some of the most commonly used protocols are:
 
 
• **Internet Protocol (IP):** It's primarily used to route packets of data from the source to the destination based on their IP addresses.
 
• **Transmission Control Protocol (TCP): **Works with IP to ensure that packets are reliably delivered. It manages error checking and retransmission of lost packets.
 
• **User Datagram Protocol (UDP): **A simpler, faster alternative to TCP that doesn't provide error checking or packet sequencing.
 
• **Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP):** The protocol used for transferring web pages and other content over the internet.
 
• **Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS): **A secure version of HTTP that provides encrypted communication and secure identification of network servers.
 
• **File Transfer Protocol (FTP):** A protocol for transferring files between systems.
 
• **Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP): **Used for sending email messages between servers.
 
• **Post Office Protocol 3 (POP3) **and **Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP)**: These are used to retrieve emails from a server.
 
• **Domain Name System (DNS): **Translates domain names into IP addresses.
 
• **Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP):** Used for managing and monitoring network devices.
 
• **Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP):** Assigns IP addresses to devices on a network.
 
• **Network Time Protocol (NTP): **Used to synchronize the clocks of computers over a network.
 
• **Secure Shell (SSH):** Allows for secure remote login from one computer to another.
 
• **Telnet**: An older protocol used for remote login. It's less secure than SSH.
 
• **Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP):** Mainly used by network devices to send error messages.
 
• **Address Resolution Protocol (ARP): **Resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses.

__
 
• ** "Loess" **is the term for** wind-deposited sediment** that is composed predominantly of silt-sized particles.
 
• **It's typically pale yellow or buff, loosely compacted, and often calcareous.**
 
• Loess deposits can be very thick, even hundreds of meters, and can blanket very large areas.
 
• It is derived from the German term **"Löss,"** which means loose or crumbly.
 
• It's found in many parts of the world, including the American Midwest, Europe, and China. The Loess Plateau in China, for example, is a well-known area of loess deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In geographical terms, a** "stack"** is a geological landform consisting of a steep and often vertical column or columns of rock in the sea near a coast, formed by wave erosion.

 
 
• **Stacks are formed over time by wind and water, processes of coastal geomorphology.**
 
• They are most commonly found in chalk or limestone areas, where the rock is softer and more prone to erosion.
 
• This process begins when the sea attacks small cracks in a headland and opens them into larger caves.
 
• If the caves are on both sides of a headland and eventually break through, they form an arch.
 
• Over time, the arch will collapse due to the force of gravity, leaving the pillar of hard rock standing away from the coast—the stack.
 
• Eventually, erosion will cause the stack to collapse, leaving a stump.Famous examples of stacks include the **Twelve Apostles in Victoria, Australia, and Old Harry Rocks in Dorset, England.**
 
 
 
• **​A moraine is a mass of rocks and sediment carried down and deposited by a glacier, typically as ridges at its edges or extremity.**
 
• There are several types of moraines, and they can give us important clues about the glacier's past behavior.
 
• Here are the main types of moraines:
 
 
• **Lateral Moraines: **These are formed at the side of the ice flow and are usually a result of frost shattering of the valley sides.
 
• **Medial Moraines:** These are formed when two glaciers merge, and lateral moraines combine to form a moraine in the middle of the glacier.
 
• **Terminal Moraines: **These mark the maximum advance of the glacier. They usually reflect the shape of the glacier's terminus.
 
• **Recessional Moraines: **These are often observed as a series of transverse ridges running across a valley behind a terminal moraine. They mark the pauses in the retreat of a glacier, where it remained stationary for enough time to produce a mound of material.
 
• **Ground Moraines:** Also called till, these are unsorted material left beneath the glacier as it melts.

Selling Price (SP) = Selling price per litre × Quantity

Profit = SP - CP

The cost price of 30 litres of milk = Rs. 50 × 30 = Rs. 1500.

He mixes 20 litres of water in it.

Total quantity of mixture = 30 + 20 = 50 litres.

Profit = Rs. (2400 - 1500) = Rs. 900.

Profit percentage = (900/1500) × 100 = 60%.

__
 
• The above-given sentence is in the active voice. We need to change it into **passive voice.**
 
• Let's look at the conversion:-
 
 
• The subject** 'He'** becomes the object **'him'** of the passive voice.
 
• The object **'****a paper****'** becomes the subject of the passive voice.
 
• Simple present tense changes in the following manner:-
 
• Active Voice - (do/does + V1) or (V1 s/es)
 
• Passive Voice - is/am/are + V3​

• Change object into subject.
 
• Change subject into object.
 
• Always use the third form of the verb in the passive voice.
 
• Use 'by' before the new object.

• *"They know they will face either a swift backlash or deafening silence."*
 
 
 
• In this sentence, all parts are properly constructed and there are no grammatical inconsistencies or errors.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] Confusion Points__ **

 
• In most cases, the use of **"a" or "the"** (indefinite or definite articles) depends on whether the noun is **countable **or **uncountable**, and whether we are referring to something specific. 

 
 
• For instance, in the case of the sentences**: "either a dog or a cat", "either a queen or a king", and "either a red card or a black card", all the nouns (dog, cat, queen, king, red card, black card) **are **countable **and not specific. Therefore, we require "a" before each of these nouns.
 
 
 
• In the case of '**deafening silence**', the **noun phrase** is treated as an **uncountable noun**. It refers to a specific type of silence, one that is loud in its quietness due to its impact or significance. Since '**silence**' is uncountable, we don't necessarily need to use '**a**' necessarily before it. Therefore, we can say "or deafening silence" after "either a swift backlash".
 
• Interestingly, depending upon the context and stylistic choice of the writer, one could also use '**a'** before '**deafening silence'**. Both these versions would be grammatically correct.
 
 
• "They know they will face either a swift backlash or **a deafening silence."**
 
• "They know they will face either a swift backlash or** deafening silence."**
